title: Local-orbital Ptychography and Its Derivatives for Ultrahigh Resolution and Robustness
content: In the fields of visible light and X-ray microscopy, computational imaging has been developed and applied widely. In recent years, computational imaging in electron microscopy has also attracted increasing attention. Its main algorithms follow the practices of visible light and X-ray imaging, representing the object function as a two-dimensional matrix composed of independent pixels. While this is a natural choice for imaging continuum, it does not take into account the discreteness or sparseness of the atomic world [1]. Based on the priori knowledge that "everything is composed of atoms," we have proposed a series of computational imaging methods based on local orbitals, including exit wave reconstruction, tomography, ptychography, and others [2-4].
